key_insight: A spatially aware hybrid Graph Neural Network combined with contrastive pretraining significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of power outage prediction under extreme weather by learning richer, topology-informed representations.
problem_solved: Predicting weather-driven power outages across distributed electrical networks where spatial dependencies, noisy/missing labels, and multimodal inputs (weather, grid topology, assets) make reliable forecasting difficult.
method: Hybrid spatial GNN that models multi-scale grid topology and neighborhood interactions to capture spatial propagation of failures.
Temporal encoder (e.g., sequence model) integrated with the GNN to handle dynamic weather and time-varying load/asset states.
Contrastive learning pretraining on multimodal inputs (weather, historical outages, sensor/asset data) to produce robust, transferable node/region embeddings for downstream outage forecasting.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to build more accurate, resilient infrastructure forecasting systems that leverage topology-aware representations and self-supervised learning—useful for transfer learning, operational decision support, and climate-resilience planning.
visual_elements: Map-based diagram showing grid topology, predicted outage hotspots, and overlayed storm track.
Schematic of the hybrid model: GNN module (spatial) + temporal encoder + contrastive pretraining flow.
Embedding space visualization (t-SNE/UMAP) comparing supervised vs. contrastive-pretrained representations.
Time-series forecast chart showing predicted vs. actual outage counts with confidence bands.
paper_title: Empowering Power Outage Prediction with Spatially Aware Hybrid Graph Neural Networks and Contrastive Learning
paper_authors: Xuyang Shen, Zijie Pan, Diego Cerrai, Xinxuan Zhang, Christopher Colorio
